answer: An economy where agents trade yarrow seeds, copper, or forecasts of a zephyr can require every identity to lock collateral for 30 days before accepting jobs. A contract slashes that collateral if the agent signs two conflicting receipts for the same job. Creating aliases is cheap, but activating each one ties up additional capital, and provable cheating burns it. Splitting a fixed stake across more names creates no extra collateral or voting weight.
